reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: write 300 roots, then read 200 computeds that walk their 3 sources — chain depth 1
reading.floor: the same writes, each marking its dependents dirty; each read is one boolean — depth 1
reading.caveat: THE ROW THE RECOVERED RUN ACTUALLY COVERED, REBUILT SO THE OTHER TWO HAVE SOMETHING TO BE READ AGAINST. Its figure at this geometry was 0.72x in our favour [NO RUN BEHIND THIS FIGURE], and the whole reason the other two rows exist is that this one was the ONLY depth measured. At depth 1 push is at its strongest: a consumer is one boolean away from knowing it owes a derivation, and the sources under it are roots, which are current by definition — so the arm has nothing to descend and nothing to bring up to date. If the recovered figure is going to reproduce anywhere it is here, and a reading far from it on this row means the two runs are not measuring the same thing and the other two rows should not be quoted either [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]. RESIDUALS. AGAINST US, AND THEY ARE THE MAJORITY: our arm is the SHIPPED `OIMComputed`, so every settle pays a call into `anySourceChangedSinceRun`, a call into `isRevisionAfter` per source, a call into the comparator, and TWO pairs of stamps written per derivation (`ranAt*` and `changedAt*`) — the rejected arm carries one boolean and writes it once. Our nodes are also filed as slots, with `effects`, `holdCount`, `owner` and `key` on every one of them, and the rejected node has none of that. AGAINST THE REJECTED ARM: nothing, except that it walks a recursive `markDependents` where a real engine might flatten it. WHAT NEITHER ARM PAYS: the frame. No effect is subscribed and `channel.flush()` is never called, so the leaf list, the drain and the after-frame phases are on neither side — a frame is priced by `flush.empty-vs-noop` and adding it to both halves of a ratio only pulls it toward 1. WHAT IS NOT EXERCISED, and it is the design difference that no timing here can show: push marks the WHOLE transitive cone at the write, while pull stops at the first computed whose value held. Every root moves every frame here and every sum therefore changes, so the comparator never cuts anything on either arm and push is never charged for a mark it did not owe. A graph where a change is absorbed part-way up is the arrangement in which push is at its worst, and it is not measured. NOR IS THE CONSUMER AXIS: the recovered table reported the two converging where ten consumers share one computed, and every node here is read by exactly one consumer.

reading.ours: the same frame over a computed reading a computed — chain depth 2
reading.floor: the same frame, marked at the write and descended by the flag — chain depth 2
reading.caveat: THE FIRST DEPTH THE RECOVERED RUN NEVER REACHED, AND THE ONE WHERE PUSH STARTS PAYING TWICE. A write now marks 200 nodes at level one and 200 more above them, and the walk is recursive; our arm's write is unchanged — it stamps a root and stops — while its READ grows by one level. So the two curves cross somewhere if they cross at all, and this row and the next are what say whether they do. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE BETWEEN THE ROWS: the population, the fan-in, the number of consumers, the writes per frame and the derive body. Only the number of levels between the roots and the consumers moves, so this row minus the depth-1 row is one level, on both arms, in one process. IF THE RATIO RISES TOWARD 1.00 AS DEPTH GROWS THE VERDICT IS NARROWER THAN THE RECOVERED TABLE CLAIMED [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE], and if it crosses 1.00 the decision is wrong for deep chains and that is the finding this file was built to be able to report. reading.ours: the same frame over a computed reading a computed reading a computed — chain depth 3
reading.floor: the same frame, marked at the write through three levels — chain depth 3
reading.caveat: THE DEPTH THE RECOVERY ENTRY NAMES BY HAND — "a computed over a computed over a computed was not measured" — and the far end of the only axis that could reverse the decision. 600 nodes now stand between 300 roots and 200 consumers. THE ARITHMETIC THE ROW IS CHECKING: push pays its marking over the whole cone at every frame's first write and then reads one boolean per node; we pay nothing at the write and one comparison per source at the read. Those are the same order of magnitude, so which wins is a question about constants and not about shapes, which is exactly the kind of question a measurement settles and an operation count does not. THIS IS THE ROW TO DISTRUST IF ANY: three levels of 200 nodes is deeper than most screens go, and a reader taking a verdict from here alone has chosen the extreme of the axis.
